Approved exact 24-slice scope, mandatory exemplar checkpoint, preservation boundary, rollback units, promotion criteria, verification cadence, and stop conditions; v2 supersedes the metadata-incomplete unstarted v1 record.

allowedWork: Define renderer-neutral presentation roles, verified plan variants, validators, law diagnostics, exact-versioned resolution, and architecture guards.
Migrate the named canonical equation bindings and generated cancellation compiler without changing mathematical truth or established motif aesthetics.
Extend stable focused, browser, visual, property, performance, and promotion checks required by the reviewed proposal.
disallowedWork: Do not add a second compositor, animation runtime, lifecycle category, or operation-specific scheduler.
Do not redesign mathematical semantics, the layout engine, or authorize LLM-authored selectors, roles, DOM, geometry, or paths.
Do not generalize beyond slice 14 until the mandatory human exemplar checkpoint is approved.
goal: Replace drifting optional equation presentation hints with one verified role-complete plan boundary, prove additive and multiplicative cancellation on fraction composition, then generalize only after human approval.
commitCadence: Commit after each independently verified slice with its exact Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop after slice 14 for explicit human approval; do not execute slices 15 through 24 before approval.
Stop if semantic roles would need to be inferred from glyph text, equality, DOM proximity, or screen geometry.
Stop if implementation requires a second compositor, animation runtime, lifecycle category, or operation-specific scheduler.
Stop if canonical transitions would retain parallel paint implementations or an implicit generic fade fallback.
Stop if inference complexity, compositor source-size, runtime performance, or bounded sampling budgets regress.
Stop if direct seek, rewind, accessibility, native endpoint authority, fold truth, or review capture regresses.
Stop if generated inputs would require authority over selectors, presentation roles, DOM, geometry, timing, or paths.
Stop if work expands to new operation semantics, a layout-engine redesign, or unlisted animation families.
Stop if durable evidence cannot be recorded or Theseus workspace validation fails.
